name: INCA33890
summary: INCA33890 is Incyte's TGFbR2xPD-1 bispecific antibody, built on Merus's Biclonics platform under the 2016 Incyte-Merus collaboration. The Phase 3 is INCA033890-303 (NCT07284849): a randomised, quadruple-blind trial of 700 patients adding INCA33890 or placebo to standard chemotherapy plus bevacizumab in untreated metastatic microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer. It excludes MSI-H/dMMR and BRAF V600E tumours, its primary endpoint is PFS, and primary completion is estimated for 2028-12-29. Price anchor: Keytruda, the PD-1 antibody labelled in first-line MSI-H colorectal cancer, at $79,464 per CMS Part B beneficiary in 2024, the price the book's PF-08634404 seed uses for the same first-line MSS colorectal pool. Uptake anchor (second reader): bevacizumab, the backbone INCA33890 must be given with, reached 57.6% of Medicare stage IV colon patients starting first-line FOLFOX or FOLFIRI in 2013 (Raab et al., Clin Colorectal Cancer 2019). A PD-1 add-on taking nivolumab's 34.7% of its backbone in first-line HER2-negative gastric cancer (Chen et al., JMCP 2026) gives 0.347 x 0.576 = 0.20 of the eligible pool. Incyte pays Merus tiered royalties of 6% to 10% of global net sales.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07284849 (book trials table, ClinicalTrials.gov last update 2026-09-15): INCA33890 or placebo added to standard-of-care chemotherapy and bevacizumab in first-line metastatic MSS colorectal cancer, randomised, quadruple-blind, primary endpoint PFS; ASCO abstract INCA033890-303 (asco.org/abstracts-presentations/266865)
therapy_mode.note: An add-on to a first-line regimen given until progression, with PFS as the primary endpoint. That is chronic by the house definition for oncology treated to progression. The registry text I could reach does not state the INCA33890 treatment cap, if there is one
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table row for NCT07284849 (fetched 2026-09-24 from ClinicalTrials.gov v2, last update 2026-09-15): design 'Randomized, Quadruple, Treatment', primary outcome PFS, 700 patients, title 'Standard-of-Care Chemotherapy and Bevacizumab With or Without INCA33890 in the First-Line Treatment of Metastatic Microsatellite Stable Colorectal Cancer'. An add-on to a first-line regimen given until progression is chronic by the brief. Amass TrialCore was unavailable (subscription limit), so the treatment cap could not be read; the ASCO abstract link was not opened.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Keytruda: CMS Medicare Part B 2024, $5,988,521,233 over 75,361 beneficiaries = $79,464 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator, following house convention. Keytruda (pembrolizumab) is the PD-1 antibody labelled in first-line colorectal cancer (MSI-H/dMMR). INCA33890 is a PD-1-based antibody for the same line, and the book's PF-08634404 seed already prices the same first-line MSS colorectal pool on this figure. Case against: a beneficiary's spend covers less than a year of therapy for many patients, so it understates an annual price. A bispecific may be priced above a PD-1 monoclonal. Bevacizumab, the backbone, is not the right anchor: at $1,632 per Part B beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Avastin), it is a biosimilar-eroded add-on
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand Keytruda: Part B 2024 total_spending $5,988,521,233 over 75,361 beneficiaries = $79,464, so 0.079464 mm USD. The PF-08634404 seed carries exactly 0.079464 on the same Keytruda Part B 2024 row. Avastin Part B 2024 = $1,632 per beneficiary, as the note says. Unit right (mm USD per patient-year). Comparator choice is a labelled judgement with its case against.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS Part B per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py). Part B pays 106% of average sales price, which is already net of discounts, so 1 - 1/1.06 comes off. Keytruda's anchor row is Part B (lookup.py demand Keytruda)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 5.66% off list, so net is $74,966 per patient-year. The PF-08634404 seed carries 0.0566 on the same anchor
gross_to_net_pct.check: Anchor is Part B (lookup.py demand Keytruda, part 'B'), so the house Part B convention applies: 1 - 1/1.06 = 0.056604, the share OFF list. backend/gross_to_net.py docstring states Part B pays 106% of ASP, so the deduction is the 6% add-on. Net = 79,464 / 1.06 = $74,966, as stated. Direction correct. PF-08634404 seed carries 0.0566.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: CheckMate 9X8 (Lenz et al., J Immunother Cancer 2024;12(3):e008409, doi:10.1136/jitc-2023-008409, PMID 38485190; NCT03414983): median PFS by BICR of 11.9 months on mFOLFOX6 plus bevacizumab in first-line mCRC. The nivolumab arm had the same median (HR 0.81)
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/11.9) = 0.503. This is the form the PF-08634404 and vepugratinib seeds use, not the brief's 1 - exp(-12/m), which treats the median as a mean. CheckMate 9X8's control arm is the same backbone as INCA033890-303's, and it is the only randomised trial of a PD-1 added to that backbone in this line. Case for higher: real-world first-line chemotherapy plus bevacizumab runs shorter. Bevacizumab-naive US patients had a median rwPFS of 8.6 months (Jin et al., Ther Adv Med Oncol 2023, doi:10.1177/17588359231182386), which gives 0.620. Immune add-ons also add toxicity stops: grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 75% vs 48% in CheckMate 9X8. Case for lower: a positive INCA33890 arm would by design extend PFS
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed PMID 38485190 (Lenz et al., J Immunother Cancer 2024, doi:10.1136/jitc-2023-008409): CheckMate 9X8, mFOLFOX6 + bevacizumab +/- nivolumab, first-line mCRC; 'median PFS by BICR was 11.9 months in both arms (HR 0.81)', grade 3-4 TRAEs 75% vs 48%. 1 - 0.5^(12/11.9) = 0.5029, recomputed. Same constant-hazard form as the PF-08634404 seed (1 - 0.5^(12/12.4) = 0.4887). The brief's 1 - exp(-12/m) would give 0.635. Case for higher checked: PMID 37360769 (Jin et al., Ther Adv Med Oncol 2023, doi:10.1177/17588359231182386): bevacizumab-awwb naive patients, median 1L PFS 8.6 months (n=129), giving 0.620.

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07284849 estimated primary completion 2028-12-29, study completion 2029-09-28 (book trials table; context file, last update 2026-09-15)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the review timeline. The book's pipeline seeds put the first full year two calendar years after the primary completion year (the ABBV-1480, telisotuzumab adizutecan and PF-08634404 seeds), which gives 2030. Case against: a completion at the very end of December leaves a readout in early 2029, a BLA around mid-2029 and a standard review to mid-2030. On that timeline 2030 is a partial launch year and 2031 the first full one
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials table: NCT07284849 primary_completion_date 2028-12-29 (estimated), completion_date 2029-09-28, start 2026-03-05. Book convention confirmed on two seeds: ABBV-1480 (primary completion December 2029 -> 2031) and telisotuzumab adizutecan (May 2029 -> 2031), both two calendar years after. 2028 + 2 = 2030. Labelled judgement with its case against (2031).

exus_multiple.source: Keytruda FY2025: $12,812mm outside the US against $18,829mm US (Merck 10-K 0000310158-26-000063; book asset_revenue_regions, sec_fsds). 12,812 / 18,829 = 0.680
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Keytruda is the price anchor and the PD-1 in this line, and the book's PF-06801591 and MK-1045 seeds use the same split. Incyte has no oncology product with a filed US/ex-US split in the book: Jakafi is US-only, with Novartis selling Jakavi abroad, and Iclusig is ex-US only. Case for lower: Incyte's own ex-US reach is thinner than Merck's. Opzelura, which Incyte sells itself in Europe, ran $130.0mm outside the US against $548.5mm US in FY2025, a ratio of 0.237 (Incyte 10-K 0000879169-26-000010). The engine scales the patient pool by 1 + this multiple, so it acts on volume
exus_multiple.check: book asset_revenue_regions, Keytruda (asset 523) FY2025: NonUs $12,812mm, US $18,829mm, sec_fsds 10-K 0000310158-26-000063; 12,812 / 18,829 = 0.6804. PF-06801591 seed carries 0.6804 and MK-1045 0.68 on the same split. Opzelura FY2025: total $678.455mm (asset_revenue), $130.0mm outside the US (asset_revenue_regions, 0000879169-26-000010), so US $548.5mm and ratio 0.237, as the note says. No Incyte oncology product carries a regional split in the book (only Opzelura, Olumiant and Jakavi rows). backend/pool_crowding.py confirms the engine multiplies the pool by 1 + exus_multiple. Web search of the trial listings reports INCA033890-303 planned at 225 sites in 23 countries, consistent with a global launch. Labelled judgement with its case against.

economics_share.source: Incyte FY2024 10-K (0001628280-25-004633), Merus collaboration note: 'For each program as to which Merus does not have commercialization or development co-funding rights, Merus is eligible to receive up to $100.0 million in future contingent development and regulatory milestones, and up to $250.0 million in commercialization milestones as well as tiered royalties ranging from 6% to 10% of global net sales'. The same terms appear in Merus's 6-K of 2016-12-21 (0001193125-16-800493, exhibit 99.1). Search of Incyte's Q2 2026 10-Q (0000879169-26-000056) returns INCA33890 described as developed by Incyte using Merus N.V.'s licensed bispecific platform. Incyte company rows (lookup.py seed on Jakafi or Opzelura, INCY FY2025): cogs 7.24%, SG&A 26.77%, R&D 39.88%, other costs 0.0%, which leave a margin of 26.11%. (0.2611 - 0.06) / 0.2611 = 0.7702
economics_share.note: Judgement: the lowest stated royalty tier, 6%. This follows the PF-08634404 seed, which takes the lowest rate its filing states. Case for lower: the tier thresholds are not disclosed, and at the top tier of 10% the share is (0.2611 - 0.10) / 0.2611 = 0.6170. Merus held an option to co-fund one specified programme, and subject to conditions a second, for 35% of development costs and 50% of US profits. I found no disclosure that it exercised that option on INCA33890. Incyte is sole sponsor of all three trials, and its filings describe the molecule as Incyte-developed. If the option had been exercised, US economics would be 0.5. Milestones of up to $350mm are not in this field. The royalty's current holder after any change of Merus's ownership does not change the rate
economics_share.check: Read the Merus note of Incyte's FY2024 10-K 0001628280-25-004633 in the book (filing_sections): 'For each program as to which Merus does not have commercialization or development co-funding rights, Merus is eligible to receive up to $100.0 million in future contingent development and regulatory milestones, and up to $250.0 million in commercialization milestones as well as tiered royalties ranging from 6% to 10% of global net sales.' The co-funding option in that filing reads 'subject to certain conditions, to co-fund development of up to two of such programs' (35% of global development costs, 50% of US profits and losses, 6% to 10% ex-US royalties), not 'one specified programme and a second' as the note paraphrases; the value is unaffected. No exercise for INCA33890 is disclosed: the FY2025 10-K 0000879169-26-000010 Merus note drops the terms entirely, the Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs (0000879169-26-000026, -000056) call INCA33890 'developed by Incyte using Merus N.V.'s licensed bispecific platform', and the Q2 2026 10-Q says Incyte opted out of MCLA-145, then the most advanced Merus programme, in January 2022. One web search of the filings found the option described but never exercised. Arithmetic: INCY rows cogs 0.0724, sga 0.2677, rd 0.3988, other 0.0 (lookup.py seed Jakafi) leave 0.2611; (0.2611 - 0.06) / 0.2611 = 0.7702; at 10%, 0.6170. Lowest-tier rule matches the PF-08634404 seed. The Merus 6-K 0001193125-16-800493 was not opened.

eligible_pct.source: Reused from the PF-08634404 seed, which covers the same first-line MSS pool. Three filters multiplied. (1) 35.1% metastatic: the telisotuzumab adizutecan seed's SEER derivation. (2) 55.9% receive chemotherapy: 47,026 of 84,161 US patients newly diagnosed with metastatic CRC, NCDB 2006-2011 (Krell et al., Cancer 2015, doi:10.1002/cncr.29253). (3) 88.6% both mismatch-repair proficient and BRAF wild-type: 2,713 of 3,063 first-line trial patients after removing 153 dMMR and 197 pMMR BRAF-mutant tumours (Venderbosch et al., Clin Cancer Res 2014, doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-0332). 0.351 x 0.559 x 0.886 = 0.1738, about 27,600 patients a year
eligible_pct.note: The filters match INCA033890-303's entry criteria. The trial takes stage IV disease not amenable to curative resection with no prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease, and excludes MSI-H/dMMR and BRAF V600E tumours (NCT07284849, as returned by search of the ClinicalTrials.gov record and site listings). Case for lower: the label will be with bevacizumab. RAS wild-type left-sided patients usually receive anti-EGFR therapy instead, and the trial also requires measurable disease and ECOG 0-1. None of these is filtered here, because I found no US share to source for them. The NCDB chemotherapy share dates from 2006-2011
eligible_pct.check: Book: PF-08634404 carries 0.1738 on Colorectal Neoplasms with the same three factors; the 35.1% metastatic derivation is on the telisotuzumab adizutecan seed. Krell et al. full text (PMC4592280, doi:10.1002/cncr.29253): '47,026 (55.9%) received chemotherapy' of 84,161 NCDB 2006-2011 metastatic CRC patients. Venderbosch et al. (PMID 25139339, doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-0332): 3,063 patients, 153 dMMR, BRAF mutant in 197 (6.8%) of pMMR tumours; 2,713 / 3,063 = 0.886. 0.351 x 0.559 x 0.886 = 0.17384; x 158,850 = 27,615. Label match: web search of the trial listings confirms first-line unresectable metastatic MSS CRC and exclusion of MSI-H/dMMR and BRAF V600E. The bevacizumab requirement is a regimen condition rather than a label population, so it is taken in penetration_peak_pct, not here, keeping this pool identical to PF-08634404's.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients
penetration_peak_pct.source: Two measured factors multiplied. (1) The reach of a bevacizumab backbone in this pool: bevacizumab, the first biologic added to first-line chemotherapy in metastatic colorectal cancer and the regimen INCA33890 is given with, was used by 57.6% of SEER-Medicare stage IV colon cancer patients starting first-line FOLFOX or FOLFIRI in 2013, down from 68.2% in 2005; 2,352 of 3,785 (62.1%) over 2005-2013 (Raab et al., Clin Colorectal Cancer 2019;18(3):e294-e299, doi:10.1016/j.clcc.2019.05.008, PMID 31266707). (2) The share of its backbone a PD-1 add-on took: nivolumab-containing regimens were 34.7% of first-line starts among 2,029 US Medicare fee-for-service patients with HER2-negative advanced gastric/GEJ cancer, 2021-2024 (Chen et al., J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2026;32(7):807-819, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2026.32.7.807, PMID 42341069). 0.347 x 0.576 = 0.1999
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement on the second factor; the first is measured in this disease, line and payer. Nivolumab's gastric label rides on fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemotherapy, which almost every first-line patient already receives, so its 34.7% is a share of its backbone. INCA033890-303 adds to chemotherapy plus bevacizumab, and in Medicare only 57.6% of first-line doublet patients get bevacizumab, so the researcher's 0.347 applied to the whole eligible pool counted patients on chemotherapy alone or anti-EGFR regimens that the label's regimen does not reach. The PF-08634404 seed's 0.20 for this pool is not a measurable anchor: its source reads only 'a share of the pool above, set against what the molecule has to displace'. Bevacizumab is the only measured first-line entrant in MSS-dominated colorectal cancer; BRAFTOVI's first-line regimen (2024) is in BRAF V600E tumours, which this trial excludes, and no uptake share was found for it. Case for higher: bevacizumab took 62.1% of its own backbone in Medicare over 2005-2013, and using that as the add-on share gives 0.576 x 0.621 = 0.358, close to the researcher's figure; nivolumab's 34.7% averages 2021-2024 including the launch year, and the PD-1 class took 44.6% in Medicare; an effective add-on could move chemotherapy-alone patients onto bevacizumab, which is now biosimilar and cheap. Using the 2005-2013 average reach gives 0.347 x 0.621 = 0.215. In all-age US data bevacizumab was still 60% (965 of 1,607) of first-line left-sided RAS/RAF wild-type patients in 2013-2018, with anti-EGFR only 12% (Nevala-Plagemann et al., J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2022, doi:10.6004/jnccn.2021.7079, PMID 35120306). Case for lower: every PD-1 tried in MSS colorectal cancer has failed, CheckMate 9X8 included; this trial's primary endpoint is PFS, where nivolumab's gastric label rested on overall survival; Raab's cohort is colon only and FOLFOX/FOLFIRI only; anti-EGFR use in left-sided RAS wild-type disease has grown since 2013; a web search summary of the trial listings describes the backbone as FOLFOX with bevacizumab, and a label restricted to an oxaliplatin backbone would narrow the reach further; PF-08634404 competes for the same patients (the book's pool_crowding module scales both if their claims exceed the pool). About 5,500 US patients a year at peak (158,850 x 0.1738 x 0.1999).
penetration_peak_pct.check: Researcher's 0.347 input confirmed on PubMed (PMID 42341069: nivolumab-containing 34.7% Medicare, 44.2% MarketScan, pembrolizumab 9.9% and 5.3%; cohort is first-line initiators 2021-2024). But the anchor is a gastric share applied to a colorectal pool without the bevacizumab-backbone constraint the researcher named and left unfiltered for want of a US share. That share exists: PubMed PMID 31266707 (Raab et al. 2019, SEER-Medicare 2005-2013) gives 62.1% (2,352 / 3,785 = 0.6214) and 57.6% in 2013; PMID 24511107 (Abrams et al., JNCI 2014, US-wide 2004-2011, all ages) gives first-line bevacizumab averaging 51%, peak 55% in 2006; PMID 22253466 (Meyerhardt et al., JCO 2012, SEER-Medicare 2002-2007 incl. pre-approval years) gives 36%. PF-08634404 anchor checked in the book (lookup.py seed): 0.2 with no incumbent or figure, so not measurable. Recomputed 0.347 x 0.576 = 0.19987. Old 0.347 -> new 0.1999.
